title: Lexical harmonizer: reconcile chat framing and tokenizer behavior during model pin onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Some newly onboarded model bundles (esp. smaller open models and certain quantized checkpoints) produce subtle subtoken splits and role-delimiter variants that break chat-template matching and cause: failed profile publish jobs, inconsistent message framing in downstream SDKs, and sporadic eval regressions. This ticket implements a lightweight 'lexical harmonizer' shim in the onboarding pipeline to normalise role delimiters, probe tokenizer boundary behavior, and emit compatibility mappings that are pinned alongside the model version. The goal is to ensure published performance profiles and runtime pins will not be invalidated by tokenizer-template mismatches.
acceptance_criteria: Onboarding pipeline runs a tokenizer probe and emits a compatibility manifest alongside the model bundle
Chat templates are automatically rewritten or annotated with stable delimiter tokens for the new model and pinned in the version metadata
Profile publish job is guarded: it will fail-fast with a clear error if delimiter mismatch probability > 0.5 unless suppressed by explicit flag
Runtime uses the compatibility manifest to coerce template framing at serve-time for pinned models, preventing divergence in published perf traces
Telemetery events appear in onboarding dashboard showing boundary mismatch rates and the population of repaired templates
implementation_steps: Add tokenizer probe step to bundle build: run representative prompt set, collect subtoken boundaries and delimiter tokens
Create a compact compatibility manifest format (delimiter, escape heuristics, whitespace collapse rules) and store with bundle metadata
Implement template harmonizer that applies safe rewrites and records diffs (keeps original templates for audit)
Integrate manifest read into profile-publish stage; add guardrails and human-readable error messages
Add unit and integration tests: multi-lingual prompts, edge cases (no-space languages, punctuation-heavy templates), and stress with long context
Feature-flag the runtime coercion behavior and rollout via canary pin for 5% of traffic before wider rollout
Document behavior in onboarding runbook and add console indicators for harmonized templates
notes: Trade-offs: the harmonizer adds a small build-time latency (seconds per bundle) and complexity in bundle metadata. We avoid aggressive token-level transformations to prevent changing semantic meaning. For high-risk customers we allow opt-out of automatic rewrites and provide a verify-only mode. We should be careful with multi-byte delimiter tokens (emoji) and languages where whitespace isn't token boundary. Follow-up: investigate applying a lighter-weight runtime prefix-canonicalizer for very latency-sensitive dedicated pools.
